messages:
jess: Hey @support — our nightly billing cron started failing with 401 invalid_api_key around 00:10 UTC. invoices didn't go out. any ideas?

samir: looking now. can you paste the exact request the job makes (curl or client snippet)?

jess: here's the curl from the cron container (we run this in a k8s CronJob):
```
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: ApiKey $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"invoice test"}'
```
response body: {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not found or malformed"}

lisa-support: quick note: our API expects `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or the `x-api-key: <key>` header. but that usually returns a different error if scheme is wrong. either way, we'll investigate both scheme and key content.

samir: can you exec into the running cron image (or run locally) and run: `echo -n "$REDWOOD_KEY" | wc -c` and `echo "$REDWOOD_KEY" | hexdump -C`? helps catch invisible chars.

jess: ran it in the job image. output:
```
# echo -n "$REDWOOD_KEY" | wc -c
58
# expected token length is 56 for our keys
# echo "$REDWOOD_KEY" | hexdump -C
00000000  61 62 63 64 65 2d 31 32  33 34 35 36 37 38 39 30  |abcde-1234567890|
00000010  61 62 63 64 65 66 67 68  39 30 31 32 33 34 35 36  |abcdefgh90123456|
00000020  0a                                                |.|
00000021
```
so there's a trailing 0a (newline). length 58 instead of 56.

samir: that explains the malformed key. common culprit is how the secret was created — often `kubectl create secret --from-file` or a Helm values block scalar can introduce a trailing newline. can you share how the secret was provisioned?

jess: we inject via Helm values.yaml: `redwood_key: |
  abcde-1234567890abcdefgh90123456` (i copied the key into the YAML with the block scalar).

lisa-support: yep the `|` block scalar preserves the trailing newline. two quick fixes:
- update Helm values to use `redwood_key: "abcde-123..."` (single-line) or use `>-` to strip final newline
- recreate the k8s secret with `kubectl create secret generic redwood-key --from-literal=key=$(echo -n "YOUR_KEY")` so no newline is included

samir: also checked our audit logs: there was a rotation event for the account jess@company.com yesterday at 23:45 UTC — if you rotated the key then the older key would be deactivated and also cause 401. can you confirm which key string you pasted into values.yaml? (new or old)

jess: ahhh i rotated the key during onboarding and then pasted the new key but used the block scalar and forgot to remove the trailing newline. i updated the Helm values to a single-line literal and redeployed the CronJob.

# after redeploy
jess: re-ran the curl from a restarted pod, now 200 OK and response payload is valid. invoices started processing again. :tada:

infra-bot: jobs/cron-billing v3.2 restarted by jess at 00:32 UTC — status: Completed

lisa-support: great — marking as resolved. two recommendations so this doesn't recur:
- prefer `--from-literal` or `echo -n` when creating k8s secrets from CI to avoid trailing newlines
- add a small startup check in the job that validates key length/charset and emits a clear log if malformed (we can share a snippet)

samir: snippet to add as a liveness precheck: `if [ "$(echo -n "$REDWOOD_KEY" | wc -c)" -ne 56 ]; then echo "ERROR: REDWOOD_KEY length unexpected"; exit 1; fi`

jess: thanks all, will add the check and update our Helm chart. great turnaround folks :thumbsup:
